column1: # Cebuano closed-class words the Wiktionary extract gets wrong or lacks (tunatale-u8nz.21).
# Hand-curated. scripts/build_cebuano_lemma_table.py makes each row THE default reading of its surface;
# Wiktionary's own readings stay, as non-defaults.
# Why: kaikki's "article" POS is not in the shared POS map, and the extract has no entry at all for
# mga, ka, si, ni, aron, usab, o — among the 20 commonest tokens in Cebuano news.
# ⚠️ wala and kini are VOCAB cards in both learners' decks (measured 2026-09-27; ka was too, until 2026-09-28). A function-word
# UPOS (ADP DET CCONJ SCONJ PART) would make a lesson treat them as clozes and stop matching those
# cards, so they get content UPOS here. Every function-word row below is either already a cloze in the
# decks or not a card at all.
# Lemmas: a surface keeps itself unless it is a contraction or case form of another word listed here.
# The last rows are not closed-class: they are default overrides for content words the same rule gets
# wrong. Wiktionary heads some affixed verbs as nouns too (nagdala "the protagonist"), and a noun headword
# keeps its own reading by default, so a lesson's nagdala never reached dala (the user, 2026-10-03). Each
# is a verb in nearly every use; the noun stays as a non-default for the context resolver. sais is the
# main spelling of six (sayis is its variant, spelling_variants.tsv), and Wiktionary has no sais at all.
# Verb headwords that are plain inflection (tunatale-ve4p.10, 2026-10-09). Wiktionary gives mogawas "to go out" an
# entry with senses of its own, and a verb headword keeps itself, so mogawas never reached gawas except where a
# lesson's context tag happened to pick the generated row. Listed by hand, not by rule: the same headword shape is
# natawo "born" (tawo "person") and managat "to fish" (dagat "sea"), which must stay themselves.
# orasa is the generator's mistake the other way: root + -a is an imperative only on a verb.
